surfaces.summary: No observed malware, credential collection, covert network calls, persistence or system command execution. Model SHA256 1102326b68da95564de147106612df71cb891b42f0726ba0212d3b9a5bcae295. Main NPZ and preflop tables contain only float32 numerical arrays.

surfaces.label: Independent baseline: runtime, opponents, packaging and tooling

resolved_questions: No malicious behavior found in fully reviewed fixed-bot runtime, all 18 benchmark/opponent bots, packaging, and reviewed training/tooling modules. No credential harvesting, covert exfiltration, persistence, mining, or obfuscated executable payload found.
Main runtime loads local NPZ files through numpy.load without enabling pickle, performs numerical inference, and returns poker actions. BOT_DATA_DIR is an owner-controlled environment setting.

All bots/**/*.py received full coverage through direct source reads or a fully reviewed base plus complete variant diffs. A truncated equity_balanced diff was supplemented by direct reading of the missing prefix.
bots/extra/cfr_kmeans_router/bot.py assigns loaded NPZ objects through globals()[_global], but _global comes exclusively from three hardcoded model names. No classifier pickle is loaded.

training/train.py:532 explicitly uses torch.load(weights_only=False) when --resume is requested and configured checkpoint_dir/latest.pt exists. This requires trusting the checkpoint, is not part of fixed-bot runtime, and is not evidence of malware. No remote-download-to-resume chain found.

Reviewed cluster and watcher process/network calls implement explicit owner-operated deployment, checkpoint pulling, local benchmarking, and HTCondor submission. The uv installer downloads from the named Astral URL only in the explicitly invoked environment setup script.
Optional vendored validator host-execution and match timeout weaknesses were handed to the separate focused reviewer; findings are omitted here to avoid duplicate reporting.
This review did not execute repository code, load pickle artifacts, install dependencies, or make network requests. Unlisted files have not received full review by this agent.

resolved_questions.question: Do training or watcher files contain covert credential collection, network access, persistence, or payload execution?
resolved_questions.resolution: No such behavior found in the 26 completely reviewed files. Training kernels implement numerical poker simulation and optimization. Watcher operations stage model files, invoke the benchmark harness, synchronize through its explicit checkpoint-sync helper, and maintain local JSON/log/plot outputs.

resolved_questions.question: Is unrestricted PyTorch deserialization reachable during bot-plus-NPZ use?
resolved_questions.resolution: No connection to bot-only execution was found. training.train explicitly loads <checkpoint-dir>/latest.pt with weights_only=False only when resume is true and the file exists. Default resume is false; command-line --resume is an opt-in training operation. An untrusted latest.pt would be dangerous, but attacker-controlled checkpoint provenance is not established, and this is not evidence of malware.

resolved_questions.question: What other deserialization and file changes occur?
resolved_questions.resolution: The trainer reads or generates repo/data/hand_eval_lut.npz and exports numeric model NPZ arrays and PT checkpoints under the operator-selected checkpoint directory. Watcher analysis uses np.load without allow_pickle=True. Watcher state uses JSON and atomic tempfile replacement, local logs, and flock locks. No unrelated personal-file enumeration or credential-file reads were present.

resolved_questions.question: Do the scripts perform hidden external actions?
resolved_questions.resolution: Python wrappers dispatch fixed repository modules. plot_benchmark.py writes a local documentation image. cluster_deploy.sh visibly sends code and selected checkpoints to its SSH argument, default yew11. cluster_build_venv.sh conditionally downloads the public Astral installer and pipes it to sh, then installs Python/dependencies. These are explicit cluster setup/deployment scripts, not imported runtime behavior. No digest verification is shown for the installer; no malicious destination or payload is established.

resolved_questions.question: Does this establish every dependency and incoming model is safe?
resolved_questions.resolution: No. This packet is offline source review, without execution or dependency implementation inspection. Numeric routines assume trainer-generated shapes and valid game arrays; malformed imported lookup arrays may crash numerical/native consumers, but no exploit or untrusted remote route was established. Baseline review owns imported benchmark, cluster and watcher CLI/sync implementations.

surfaces.label: Optional submission validation and match execution

originalCandidates.control: bot submission author controls bot.py passed to validate/CLI
originalCandidates.counterevidence: Requires operator passing attacker-controlled submission; tests/test_smoke.py uses fixed repository bot. Docker controls in match.py do not cover validator. No public remote submission endpoint identified.
originalCandidates.evidence: check_static lines221-227 allows from os import system because os is permitted; lines258-280 only reject selected Name calls and attributes spelled os.*. A top-level system(...) via imported alias passes these checks. validate lines523-534 then load_bot exec_module line347 executes it directly in host process, before any Docker sandbox. CLI570 and Makefile19 reach this path.
originalCandidates.impact: An operator validating an untrusted bot grants host-user code execution, files/environment/network access; this is a validator vulnerability, not evidence shipped bot is malware.
originalCandidates.remediation: Do not treat AST blacklist as security boundary; run import and decide validation only inside independently killed isolated worker/container without host secrets or writable host mounts; keep static checks as lint only.

originalCandidates.control: untrusted submitted bot controls import-time behavior and stdout/stderr in runner
originalCandidates.counterevidence: Ordinary decide exceptions/timeouts are handled by runner103-123. Fixed trusted runtime does not expose arbitrary submission author capability; no claim of container escape.
originalCandidates.evidence: Parent warmup/read and act use blocking readline without deadline (187,161). runner main76 imports bot before timed _call_with_timeout103; top-level loop/sleep never reaches warmup timeout. run_match239-240 invokes warmup before try/finally242, so cleanup is not reached. Docker CPU/memory limits121-129 do not impose wall-clock deadline.
originalCandidates.impact: A submitted bot can hang a match indefinitely even with USE_DOCKER=true; CLI360 and demo.py286/341 have no outer timeout. Unconsumed stderr PIPE also permits backpressure; primary finding is import/warmup boundary.
originalCandidates.remediation: Enforce host-side startup and per-response wall-clock deadlines; bounded framed output and drained capped stderr; kill/reap container using owned ID, and include startup/warmup inside cleanup finally.
